description: Na₃Fe₂(PO₄)₃ crystallizes in the monoclinic P2₁/c space group. There are three inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.20-2.61 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.22-2.66 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.22-2.79 Å. There are two inequivalent Fe sites. In the first Fe site, Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with six PO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.94-2.37 Å. In the second Fe site, Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with six PO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.92-2.23 Å. There are three inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four FeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 25-40°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.54-1.56 Å. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four FeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 7-40°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.53-1.57 Å. In the third P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four FeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 20-37°. There is one shorter (1.53 Å) and three longer (1.56 Å) P-O bond lengths. There are twelve inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted T-shaped geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a bent 150 degrees geometry to one Fe and one P atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a linear geometry to one Fe and one P atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the tenth O site, O is bonded in a distorted T-shaped geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the eleventh O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the twelfth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one P atom.
